_comment: CANONICAL namespace -> api bucket mapping. Authoritative for v1.4.6 / v1.4.7 / v1.5.3 content trees. Boss-owned artifact; Leads apply it verbatim instead of inventing per-version directory maps. One type = exactly one path, no duplicates.
why: The legacy v1.4.5 tree is NOT a safe source of truth: 2199 type names are duplicated across buckets (every TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem type exists in both campaign/ and campaign-ext/), and 171 of 513 namespaces are split across buckets. Counting pages there yields nonsense (TaleWorlds.InputSystem -> campaign-ext, TaleWorlds.DotNet -> campaign-ext). So the bucket taxonomy is fixed by the subsystem table below, not by legacy page counts.
matchSemantics: longest-prefix-wins. Do NOT use first-match. The array below is ALSO physically sorted so that first-match and longest-match give the same answer; if you add a rule, keep it sorted by descending prefix length. Rationale: TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.CustomBattle and TaleWorlds.*.ViewModelCollection must beat their shorter parent prefixes.
collisionRule: If two namespaces mapping to the SAME dir export the same simple type name, the page file is <NamespaceLeaf>__<TypeName>.md (e.g. Campaign__IFaction.md). Never write two files for one type.

entryPointDirs._match: exact simple type name, case-sensitive, compared AFTER longest-prefix resolution
entryPointDirs._why: Everything else was a no-op or contradicted 1.4.5 on-disk precedent. Measured 1.4.5 zh buckets: TextObject->localization (NOT core-extra), MBDebug->engine (NOT core-extra), GameModels->campaign (NOT core-extra), ViewModel/Game/GameStateManager/GameManagerBase/MBGameModel->core-extra, ScreenManager/ScreenBase/ScreenLayer->gui, GauntletLayer->engine, Save*->save-system. Those are all already produced by the prefix rules, so they need no override. Hyphenated/space-containing entries were unmatchable dead weight and are gone.
entryPointDirs._parityGaps: MissionState lands in mission/ here but 1.4.5 has it duplicated in campaign-ext/+mission-ext/, not mission/ - 1 URL parity gap, accepted for modder-facing grouping. ModuleManager is NOT overridden: no 1.4.5 precedent exists, so it stays in modulemanager/ per its own prefix rule (one fewer override = one fewer silent failure).
entryPointDirs._noModuleManager: There is NO ModuleManager type in any version: verified by full-tree scan of 1.4.5 (8583 .cs), 1.4.6 (11385), 1.4.7 (11387), 1.5.3 (11487) - zero occurrences of a class/struct/interface named ModuleManager, and 1.4.5 has no ModuleManager.md page. The modulemanager/ bucket holds the OTHER types of the TaleWorlds.ModuleManager namespace (DependedModule, Extensions, IPlatformModuleExtension, ModuleCategory, ModuleHelper, ModuleInfo, ModuleType, SubModuleInfo). Never synthesize a ModuleManager page.

resolutionOrder: 1. excludeNamespaces / excludeSuffixes / sourceTypoNamespaces  -> hard skip, no page, counted separately
2. rules[] -> longest-prefix-wins. Record the matched rule (dirRule) but DO NOT return early.

3. entryPointDirs -> override by exact case-sensitive simple type name. This step runs for EVERY type, including those whose namespace already matched a prefix rule in step 2. If no override matches, keep the step-2 result.
4. defaultDir (core-extra) if step 2 matched nothing AND step 3 has no entry -> also record in unmapped
_excludeNote: Shared noise gate so all three new versions use ONE filter instead of three divergent ones. Measured on 1.5.3: 96 namespaces fall through the business rules and would otherwise be dumped into core-extra, polluting the bucket and corrupting gap accounting. Report deviations from this list instead of silently diverging.
_sourceTypoNote: Typos in TaleWorlds' own source (Sandbox vs SandBox, Sandobx, Storymode). Ruled: EXCLUDE, do not map to sandbox/storymode - mapping would invent a namespace rule the source does not support. Listed here so the affected types are accounted for rather than silently dropped.

parityGaps.reason: The 1.4.5 gameplay/ bucket is semantically mixed: it holds SandBox(4), StoryMode.*(4) and bare TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade types (AgentNavigator, MapAudioManager, OppositionData, DelayedAction, NameplateSize, ...). No namespace rule can reproduce it. Bucket deliberately NOT created - SandBox* -> sandbox and StoryMode* -> storymode, which match the real namespaces.
parityGaps.decision: accept the 19-URL break; do not invent a bucket to make numbers line up

parityGaps.reason: 52 of 1.4.5's 78 mission/ pages are bare TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade types (Agent, Formation, ActionIndexCache, AutoGeneratedSaveManager, BannerTextureCreator, AgentHelper, GenericMissionObjective, ...). That is a hand-picked modder entry list no namespace rule can reproduce; faking parity would mean shredding the ~850-page mission-ext bucket and hand-maintaining a list.
parityGaps.decision: accept; mission/ stays a small intentional entry-class carve-out with bidirectional links to ../mission-ext/

parityGaps.reason: Game is namespace TaleWorlds.Core, which the prefix rules route to core-extra. 1.4.5 happens to keep a copy in core/ (and a duplicate in core-extra/).
parityGaps.decision: accept the 1-URL move; namespace consistency beats copying a legacy duplicate

parityGaps.reason: 1.4.5 has MissionState duplicated in campaign-ext/ and mission-ext/ and no mission/ copy. The entryPointDirs carve-out groups it with Mission/Agent/Formation for modders.
parityGaps.decision: accept the 1-URL break for modder-facing grouping

parityGaps.reason: 1.5.3 has no TaleWorlds.BoardGames namespace (grep 0 hits); the 43 board-game types live in SandBox.BoardGames* child namespaces, which the SandBox -> sandbox rule already routes to sandbox/.
parityGaps.decision: do not create an empty bucket; a rule that can never match plus a permanently empty bucket is exactly the silent failure the non-empty assertion exists to catch

_parseContract: FAIL-CLOSED. Consumers MUST assert schemaVersion===5 and MUST error on any unknown shape. Never silently ignore an unrecognised key. v5 aligns excludeSuffixes with handwritten-policy.mjs (numeric-suffixed AutoGenerated) and records _exclusionAlignment.

linkRules._principle: Links are resolved ROUTE-relative: every page route is its own directory, so one '..' pops exactly one path segment. fs.existsSync on the joined path is NOT a valid check - wrong-level links exist as files.
forbidden: content/ anywhere in an href - repo-root-relative leakage
a version segment inside a SAME-version link
../<bucket>/<Name> from a leaf page - one level short, only reachable as a sibling
./<Name> from a leaf page - dot-slash is legal only from a bucket _index.md
linkRules.evidence: shipped v1.4.5 zh/api uses 2+ '../' for 5215 cross-bucket links; the generated 1.4.7 tree emitted only 40 such links and 4135 one-'../' links carrying a bucket name, which is the defect signature
linkRules.gate: For every emitted relative link: route(from) = the page's own route ending in '/'; target = normalize(route(from) + href) popping one segment per '..' and dropping '.'; assert exists(content/<target>.md) || exists(content/<target>/_index.md). PLUS a complementary reverse assertion on forbidden substrings - depth-only checks cannot see a wrong prefix, and a fix that satisfies the check which caught the previous bug can satisfy it while introducing a different bug.
linkRules.popToSiteRoot: pops-to-site-root == number of segments in the page's OWN route. A leaf route v1.4.7/zh/architecture/version-delta/ has 4 segments and needs FOUR '../'; a section-index route v1.4.7/zh/architecture/ has 3 and needs THREE. Same-version links never need this (they stay inside the tree); cross-version links climb to the site root and therefore need the full pop count.
linkRules.crossVersion: ../ x(popToSiteRoot) / <version> / <lang> / <section> / <Name>. The language segment must match the TARGET tree, not the source. Verified correct: leaf -> ../../../../v1.4.5/zh/architecture/ ; index -> ../../../v1.4.5/zh/architecture/
linkRules._forbiddenNote: Refined from a blanket rule after lead-2 proved it wrong: 'no v1. in any href' would ban the ONLY correct form of a cross-version link, and would have flagged 6 genuinely-broken links as rule-compliant while leaving them broken. It mistakes the symptom for the disease. A cross-version href legitimately contains a version segment; what is forbidden is a version segment inside a SAME-version link.

_resolutionPseudocode: let dir = longestPrefixMatch(ns); dir = dir || defaultDir; // step 2 - NO early return
if (entryPointDirs[typeName]) dir = entryPointDirs[typeName]; // step 3 - ALWAYS runs
_resolutionWarning: Step 3 must NOT be guarded by 'only if step 2 found nothing'. An implementation that returns as soon as a prefix rule matches will silently produce mission=0 and core=0, because the rule TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade -> mission-ext claims all 7 override targets first. Overrides are consulted on every type, so both 'override-first' and 'prefix-then-override' produce identical output; the documented order is kept only because override-first is name-based and will misroute the day a second Agent or Module appears in another namespace. Expected result: mission=5, core=2.

_deadRulesRemoved.verified: grep `namespace TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.PartyBasedVisitables` -> 0 hits across all 6 version trees (1.3.0/1.3.15/1.4.5/1.4.6/1.4.7/1.5.3)
_deadRulesRemoved.foundBy: lead-1 worker-43, cross-checked by lead-4 sampling, independently re-verified by Boss
_deadRulesRemoved.consequence: it routed nothing; any page still claiming a campaign-ext `PartyBasedVisitables` namespace was mis-bucketed. NOTE bare `SandBox` -> sandbox is a SEPARATE, LIVE rule and was kept.

_deadRulesRemoved.verified: grep `namespace TaleWorlds.CampaignSystem.SandBox` -> 0 hits across all 6 version trees
_deadRulesRemoved.consequence: same as above; the real namespaces are `StoryMode.Missions`, `StoryMode.Quests.*`, `StoryMode.GameComponents`, and `SandBox.*` (top-level, covered by the live `SandBox` rule).

_exclusionAlignment.note: Namespace segments can carry a numeric suffix that the source DIRECTORY does not.
_exclusionAlignment.consequence: 855 auto-generated GauntletUI binding types were counted in the gap denominator. Removing them changes the DENOMINATOR, not real progress.
_exclusionAlignment.alignedWith: tools/lib/handwritten-policy.mjs which matches ^AutoGenerated\d*$ on the namespace segment
_exclusionAlignment.reportingRule: When the denominator changes, every gap report must state the old and new denominator. A smaller gap is NOT progress if the denominator shrank.
